steps.title: Foundations
lines: Using AI, we process and measure information about industries and markets from source material, scoring it across various dimensions.

steps.title: Defining the landscape
lines: The **height** of each peak shows how much credible evidence backs it across our sources; its **width** shows how often it's mentioned.

steps.title: Controlling impact
lines: Lots of evidence from a single source has a **diminishing impact**, but supporting evidence from multiple sources has a **greater impact**.

steps.title: Two views
lines: In the first view, each hill represents an industry, its size informed by the **markets it contains**.
The second view reveals **all markets**, each one a peak of its own.

steps.title: Positioning
lines: Peaks in the same industry gather together, so the closer two peaks are, **the more they have in common**.

steps.title: Growing the landscape
lines: As more documents are added and we learn new insights, **emerging industries and markets** appear on the map, and existing ones will be updated.

steps.title: Uniquely yours
lines: No two landscapes are alike. Adding your brand's own data further elevates insight and helps us spot **opportunities** and understand a world that is truly yours.

blocks.p: This notice is for the people who sign in to the Pathways portal, and for anyone who takes part in a Pathways workshop by joining on their phone. It says what we hold about you, why, and for how long.

Parallel runs the portal with &go&co, our method partner, as one team, for your organisation and under our agreement with it. Your organisation decides who may sign in. To reach us about your data, ask the person at your organisation who invited you.

blocks.p: That's all for the portal: there are no passwords, and no analytics, advertising or tracking.

blocks.h: If you take part in a workshop

blocks.p: You join a workshop on your phone with a code, without signing in. When you take part, we hold:

ul: Your first name and your team

(brand, product or research). Your name shows on the big screen while people join and place. It's deleted when the facilitator saves the session, or 7 days after the session was set up if it's never saved.
Your placements on the workshop's grids, and any line of why you add.

The room sees them in your team's colour, never with your name, and they're saved with your team, never your name. If you're the only one from your team, people in the room may be able to tell which are yours.

blocks.p: Cloudflare Access sets only the cookies it needs to sign you in and keep you signed in, such as CF_Authorization. None are for analytics or advertising. A sign-in lasts up to 24 hours; then you sign in again.
The map also remembers a few display choices in your browser, such as the colour scale and how far you've got in How it works. They stay on your device and are never sent to us.
If you join a workshop, your phone remembers your name, team and answers for that session, so a reload picks up where you left off. They're cleared from it when the session ends.

ul: To let only the people your organisation has approved in.
To keep the portal and your organisation's information secure, and to look into misuse.
To run workshops your organisation has asked us for, and keep a record, by team, of where the room placed your brand.

blocks.p: We do this because we have a legitimate interest in keeping the portal secure, and to provide the service your organisation has asked us for, its workshops included. We don't use your data for anything else, and we don't sell it or share it with anyone else.

ul: Our team: Parallel and &go&co. Only Parallel's admins manage who can sign in.
Cloudflare, which runs the portal and its sign-in for us and stores your data in North America, under its data protection terms. It's listed under Services we use.

blocks.p: The portal and the workshop run no AI, and send nothing about you to any AI service.

ul: Your portal account: until 12 months after the engagement ends, or sooner if your organisation asks.

Workshop results (placements and lines of why by team, and evidence requests with their owner's role): until 17 January 2027, then deleted, with any copies our team downloaded. Cloudflare's backups can restore deleted data for up to 30 days after that. Names never outlast the session.
Cloudflare's sign-in records: for a short period, under Cloudflare's terms.

blocks.p: You can ask to see, correct or delete what we hold about you, or object to or limit how we use it. Ask the person at your organisation who invited you. You can also complain to your data protection regulator: in the UK, the Information Commissioner's Office.
